A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAD research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v2 reports original jailbreak-defense and general-QA experiments in Tables 1–3, plus appendix experiments on robustness, component choices, latency, and database scaling.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds component-removal results, latency measurements across configurations, and qualitative adaptation and failure cases.

M1.justification: Both versions retain the Retrieve–Rerank–Extract–Classify–Vote pipeline, PMI/likelihood reranking, majority/weighted voting, and threshold-based refusal. v3 expands the PMI explanation and evaluates component removals as ablations without revising the proposed RAD method.

E1.justification: Both retain StrongREJECT, its synthesized benign counterpart, AdvBench/DAN/HarmBench seed queries, MMLU, AlpacaEval 2.0, and the same attack families and attacker-model coverage. The new ablations and cases remain within these existing tasks and conditions.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Self-Reminder, Llama Guard 3, Intention Analysis, and Safety Context Retrieval alongside RAD and No Defense. Table 3 retains the same QA comparators. The new removed-component configurations constitute an additional RAD ablation series.

E3.justification: v3 adds latency experiments for retrieval/reranking sizes (20,5), (20,10), (50,5), and (50,10). New ablation protocols retrieve ten items without reranking, omit the extracted-query classifier input, or retrieve one item without ensemble voting. Existing evaluation settings and default sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v2's scoring/voting-choice ablation, v3 tests removal of entire Rerank, Extract, and Vote steps in Table 8, adds latency sensitivity in Table 7, and introduces adaptation and failure cases in Appendix N. This substantially expands analysis of component contributions and errors. Table 11 changes prompts between conditions, limiting causal attribution.

E5.justification: The five-seed DAN setup, Template/DAN confidence-interval reporting, AlpacaEval uncertainty reporting, and Table 6 latency uncertainties are retained. New ablation win-rates extend the existing plus/minus reporting; no revised run count or new statistical estimation procedure is documented.

E6.justification: All existing table values and plotted results are retained; v2 Tables 7 and 8 become v3 Tables 9 and 10. Added supplementary outcomes include latency and case outputs. New Table 8 reports FRR of 10.86% without Extract versus 1.28% for full RAD-Sim, and PAP scores of 59.50 without Vote versus 35.22 for full RAD-Sim.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the PMI filtering rule, and the FRR-budget formulation remain unchanged. The added discussion of positive, zero, and negative PMI explains the existing definition without adding a formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free adaptation, strong jailbreak defense, utility preservation, and controllable safety–utility trade-offs. The supplementary evidence does not redefine those claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations of component-removal trade-offs, PMI filtering, adaptation through improved intent extraction, and failures from aggregation or classifier sensitivity. Appendix N's false-positive discussion emphasizes classification, whereas Table 12's caption emphasizes extraction. The earlier main interpretations and dedicated Limitations section remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The code/data access pointer changes from an anonymous repository to the authors' RAD project page. v3 also documents the component-removal implementations and runtime breakdowns for additional retrieval/reranking sizes. Appendix C's software versions, hardware, models, and default settings are retained.

R1.justification: The reference list, Section 2, and related-work comparisons in Appendices F–G are unchanged. No cited research is added or removed, and RAD's positioning relative to RePD, EDDF, and SCR is retained.

P1.justification: v3 adds a localized PMI explanation, appendix cross-references, acknowledgments, and qualitative Appendix N; AI Assistance moves from N to O. Most existing prose and section organization remain intact. The new failure discussion repeats its false-negative description.

P2.justification: v3 adds appendix Tables 7, 8, 11, and 12 for latency configurations, component removals, and qualitative cases. Existing tables are retained with some relocation and renumbering, while text and floats reflow. All four figures retain their drawings, axes, legends, and plotted content.

improvement.justification: Tables 7–8 and Appendix N provide useful evidence about component contributions, runtime sensitivity, and concrete failures that v2 lacked. These additions modestly improve diagnostic depth while the central results remain unchanged. The benefit is limited by Table 11's changed prompts and repetition and differing caption/text explanations in the failure analysis, but the added ablation and failure evidence supports a small net improvement.
